children: SB Energy, a developer of integrated data center and power infrastructure, filed for an initial public offering. The company plans to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market and Nasdaq Texas under the ticker “SBE.” Proceeds will fund data center and power project development, working capital, and potential debt repayment.

SB Energy develops, builds and plans to operate gigawatt-scale, power-integrated data center campuses alongside utility-scale power assets. The company’s vertically integrated model spans site origination, grid interconnection, on-site and grid-connected power, data center design and construction management, and long-term operations, allowing it to offer turnkey, triple-net leased facilities to hyperscalers and AI labs and sell electricity through long-term power purchase agreements. Its revenue model comprises data center leasing, power offtake (including energy, capacity and renewable attributes) and internal solutions services that support execution across both segments. As of the filing, SB Energy has 8.8 GW-IT of contracted data center capacity (0.8 GW-IT under construction and 8.0 GW-IT contracted at the PORTS-Pike Technology Campus) and a standalone power portfolio of approximately 2.2 GW of operating solar and battery storage with an additional ~2.5 GW under construction and ~0.8 GW contracted but not yet under construction. Strategic relationships include OpenAI and SoftBank as anchor tenants at multiple campuses and a residual value guaranty from NVIDIA covering an initial 4.25 GW-IT at PORTS-Pike, which is designed to be among the world’s largest data center developments. The company focuses on “power-first” development to compress delivery timelines and improve cost certainty in a market constrained by grid bottlenecks and long-lead electrical equipment.
